title: Indrajit's death
hook: an uncle and a nephew face each other at the fire, and Lakshmana makes a vow on his brother's name

segments.voice: Yesterday: Indrajit's death began with an illusion, a magic Sita cut down to stop the army, and Vibhishana saying look again. Did you separate a fear from the facts? Today, the race reaches Nikumbhila. Day six hundred fifty-three.

The grove at Nikumbhila is dark with trees, and somewhere inside, a fire is burning. Lakshmana's army crashes into the rakshasas guarding it, and the fighting gets so loud and close that Indrajit has to leave his offering unfinished and come out. He climbs into his chariot. And the first face he sees in the enemy line isn't Lakshmana's. It's his uncle's. Vibhishana, who knew about the fire, and the grove, and the secret condition, and who brought them here.
screen: `THE FIRE IN THE GROVE.` → `THE RITE LEFT UNFINISHED.` → `HIS UNCLE'S FACE.`

segments.voice: Indrajit's words to Vibhishana are bitter. You were born here, he says, you're my father's brother, and you've brought the enemy to your own nephew. You've thrown away your family and your people to serve strangers. Vibhishana answers without shouting. I was born among the rakshasas, he says, but my nature isn't cruel. I didn't leave my brother because I hate him. I left because what he was doing was wrong, and I couldn't take part in it. Both of them are speaking from loyalty; they just mean different things by it. Then the duel begins, Lakshmana and Indrajit, and Valmiki makes it long and close: chariots wrecked, armor split, both men bleeding, neither giving way. At last Lakshmana fits to his bow the weapon of Indra, the king of the gods. And before he lets it go, he speaks a vow. If Rama, son of Dasharatha, is righteous, and true to his word, and unmatched in courage, then let this arrow kill Ravana's son. The arrow flies, and Indrajit falls. Listen to the shape of that vow. Lakshmana doesn't rest the arrow on his own strength. He rests it on his brother's goodness. And the warrior named conqueror of Indra is brought down, at last, by Indra's own weapon. In Lanka, Ravana hears and loses his mind with grief. He grabs his sword and rushes toward the ashoka grove to kill Sita. A minister named Suparshva steps in front of him. You, a learned king, would kill a woman? Fight Rama instead. Ravana turns back.
screen: `YOU BETRAYED YOUR FAMILY.` · `MY NATURE ISN'T CRUEL.` · `A VOW ON RAMA'S GOODNESS.` · `SUPARSHVA STOPS THE SWORD.` · then, large: `BROUGHT DOWN BY INDRA'S OWN WEAPON.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably. Think of someone whose goodness you trust completely. A parent, a teacher, a friend. Lakshmana put his whole weight on his brother's goodness. Picture this person, and let yourself lean on them for a moment, in your mind. Breathe in their steadiness. Breathe out, and feel a little less alone in whatever you're facing. The bell holds the time.
Indrajit's death. At Nikumbhila, his rite broken, he falls to Lakshmana's arrow of Indra, shot on a vow resting on Rama's goodness.
Your line: Indrajit's death. Today, lean on one person whose goodness you trust, and tell them. Day six hundred fifty-three.

howItsDone: Lakshmana's vow before the final arrow, resting on Rama's righteousness and truth, is often quoted by Ramayana teachers as a picture of Lakshmana's devotion to his brother.

myth: Indrajit finishes his rite before the battle
the attack forces him to leave it unfinished.
Lakshmana's vow rests on Rama's goodness, not his own strength
if Rama is righteous and true, let this arrow kill Ravana's son.
after Indrajit's death, Ravana sets out to kill Sita
his minister Suparshva stops him and turns him toward Rama.

fork.setup: you're Lakshmana. the duel has gone on and on, and you're both wounded. you take up Indra's weapon. what do you do before you shoot?
options: speak a vow on Rama's goodness.
offer Indrajit one last chance to surrender.
fork.reveal: he vows: if Rama is righteous, true and unmatched in courage, let this arrow kill Ravana's son; and it does.

original.note: Sanskrit aindrāstra: the weapon of Indra, from aindra, belonging to Indra, and astra, weapon.

trapdoor: what you thought: Lakshmana simply outfought Indrajit.
what it means: he shot Indra's weapon on a vow resting on Rama's righteousness.
what a scholar hears: the irony is Valmiki's: the warrior named conqueror of Indra falls to Indra's own weapon.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 86–87 (Nikumbhila; Indrajit and Vibhishana)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.

Lakshmana's vow (dharmātmā satyasandhaś ca rāmo dāśarathir yadi / pauruṣe cāpratidvandvas tadainaṃ jahi rāvaṇim): paraphrased in English; confirm the verse.
Suparshva's words to Ravana: paraphrased; confirm.
Indrajit's death kept unspecific (Valmiki: the arrow severs his head).
